articles.title: Why is my ecobee thermostat rebooting?
articles.description: Explains why an ecobee thermostat may reboot or lose power, including HVAC power interruptions, heating and cooling issues, and transformer sizing concerns.

articles.title: Troubleshooting Furnace Heating Issues
articles.description: Troubleshoots furnace and heat pump heating issues on ecobee thermostats, including wiring, configuration, airflow, and overheating.

articles.title: Troubleshooting Cooling Issues
articles.description: Troubleshoots common cooling issues on ecobee thermostats, including test mode checks, system mode, wiring, free cooling, and condensate problems.

articles.title: How to troubleshoot ecobee thermostat power issues
articles.description: Troubleshoots black-screen and power issues on ecobee thermostats, including wiring, PEK setup, HVAC power, fuse checks, heating, and cooling failures.

chunks.content: The ecobee thermostat has no internal power source. It is powered by HVAC equipment, so if that equipment has no power, the ecobee will not power on. If the thermostat frequently loses power or displays a calibrating message, the issue is usually related to interruptions in the 24VAC power supply.
chunks.title: Why is my ecobee thermostat rebooting?

chunks.content: Interruptions to the 24VAC power supply can cause the thermostat to go black or reboot during heating or cooling calls. HVAC safety features such as a high-limit switch or float switch may cut power to prevent equipment damage. An inadequate transformer VA rating can also cause power loss, especially when multiple thermostats and zone valves are calling for heat.
chunks.title: Why is my ecobee thermostat rebooting?

chunks.section_title: Using System Monitor to confirm power loss
chunks.content: The ecobee System Monitor can help determine when and possibly why the thermostat lost power. Power loss usually appears as gaps in runtime reports. For cooling-related reboots, a gap in data is often preceded by a cooling call, or the inside temperature is lower when data resumes. For heating-related reboots, a gap in data is often preceded by a heating call, or the inside temperature is higher when data resumes.
chunks.title: Why is my ecobee thermostat rebooting?

chunks.content: If the system uses a furnace for heating or auxiliary heating, overheating may be the cause. When a furnace overheats, built-in safety equipment may shut off heating or power to avoid damage, while the blower fan may continue running to cool the unit. Once the furnace cools down, both the furnace and the ecobee typically power back on.
chunks.title: Why is my ecobee thermostat rebooting?

chunks.content: Common causes include reduced airflow from clogged air filters or blocked air intake, dirt and carbon buildup that requires servicing and cleaning, and long heating runs caused by aggressive temperature increases in very cold weather. Regular filter maintenance, furnace cleaning, and smaller temperature adjustments can help reduce overheating issues.
chunks.title: Why is my ecobee thermostat rebooting?

chunks.section_title: Good to know about gas and propane furnaces
chunks.content: For furnaces that use gas or propane, the burner circuit and power circuits are often separate. In that case, the ecobee may continue requesting heat while the furnace does not respond until it has cooled sufficiently. The same can apply to heat-only ecobee installations that use an external transformer.
chunks.title: Why is my ecobee thermostat rebooting?

chunks.section_title: Boiler or zone valve heating systems
chunks.content: Many boiler and zone valve systems, especially older ones, do not have a 24VAC transformer with enough VA rating to support one or more smart thermostats. For most boiler systems, a separate 24V 40VA transformer is required for the ecobee. In zone valve systems with more than three zones, a separate 24V 40VA transformer is also required.
chunks.title: Why is my ecobee thermostat rebooting?

chunks.content: If the issue happens during cooling, check whether the HVAC system is draining properly. As the air conditioner runs, moisture forms around the evaporator coils and drains into a drip pan. Under normal conditions, the water exits through the condensate drain line. If the drain line is blocked or clogged, water can build up in the drip pan and trigger float switches or condensate pumps to cut power to the HVAC system. Once the water drains, the HVAC system and ecobee usually power back on.
chunks.title: Why is my ecobee thermostat rebooting?

chunks.content: Clear the condensate lines and make sure debris is not blocking water flow. Also check and replace or clean clogged air filters regularly, since dirt and debris buildup can cause the HVAC system to overheat. If the issue continues, consult the HVAC system manual or contact an HVAC contractor for more complex diagnosis and repair.
chunks.title: Why is my ecobee thermostat rebooting?

chunks.content: This article helps troubleshoot common heating issues on an ecobee thermostat. When the thermostat is requesting heating, the flame icon will usually be orange or an orange line will appear around the perimeter depending on the model.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting Furnace Heating Issues

chunks.section_title: When ecobee is not requesting heat
chunks.content: If the thermostat is not requesting heating even though the temperature is below the setpoint, first confirm that it can request heating by using Test Mode on the thermostat.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting Furnace Heating Issues

chunks.content: For a furnace-only system, select Heat Stage 1 On for two minutes and check the vents for airflow and warm air.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting Furnace Heating Issues

chunks.content: For a heat pump system, select Heat Pump Heat Stage 1 On for two minutes to confirm the outdoor unit is running and warm air is coming from the vents. If auxiliary heat is available, select Aux Stage 1 On for two minutes and check for airflow and warm air.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting Furnace Heating Issues

chunks.content: If heating works during Test Mode, confirm the thermostat is set to Auto, Heat, or Aux system mode. Also check whether the Heat Differential has been reached, since the home temperature must fall below the setpoint by the configured amount before heating is requested.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting Furnace Heating Issues

chunks.content: For heat pump systems without auxiliary heat, check the Compressor Min Outdoor Temperature threshold. If the outdoor temperature is below this threshold, the heat pump will not be asked to run. On most ecobee models, this setting is found under Main Menu > General Settings > Settings > Installation Settings > Thresholds > Compressor Min Outdoor Temperature. On Smart Thermostat Lite and Essential models, it is found under Main Menu > Settings > Installation Settings > Thresholds > Compressor Min Outdoor Temperature.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting Furnace Heating Issues

chunks.section_title: When there is no airflow or no heat option
chunks.content: If the ecobee is requesting heat but there is no airflow from the vents or no Heat option appears, first inspect the wiring. Remove the thermostat from the wall, gently check that each wire is secure, and reseat any loose wire by pressing the tab, sliding the wire out, and reinserting it. If no wires are loose, take a photo of the wiring and reinstall the thermostat.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting Furnace Heating Issues

chunks.content: Check the thermostat configuration under Main Menu > General Settings > Settings > Installation Settings > Equipment > Wiring. The highlighted wires should match the wiring behind the thermostat. If they do not match, exit Wiring and choose Reconfigure Equipment. On Smart Thermostat Lite and Essential models, the path is Main Menu > Settings > Installation Settings > Equipment > Wiring.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting Furnace Heating Issues

chunks.section_title: If wiring and configuration are correct but the home is still not heating
chunks.content: For heat pump systems, confirm the manufacturer-recommended operating temperatures, since heat pumps can struggle when the outdoor temperature drops to the cutoff or balance point. If the Compressor Min Outdoor Temperature threshold was lowered or disabled, consider restoring the manufacturer's recommended setting or the ecobee default of 35F / 1.7C. Check the heat pump manual or the specification sticker on the unit for the recommended values.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting Furnace Heating Issues

chunks.content: For furnace heating issues, first check that the furnace breaker at the main panel has not tripped. Then inspect the furnace or air handler for error codes, indicator lights, or light patterns and refer to the furnace manual for meaning and resolution.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting Furnace Heating Issues

chunks.content: If the furnace is overheating, built-in safety equipment may shut off heating or power to prevent damage while the blower fan continues cooling the furnace. Electric furnaces may shut off power entirely, which also turns off the ecobee if it is powered by the furnace. Gas or propane furnaces often keep burner and power circuits separate, so ecobee may keep requesting heat while the furnace waits to cool. Common causes include restricted airflow from dirty filters, dirt and carbon buildup, and long heating runs in very cold weather.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting Furnace Heating Issues

chunks.content: If the issue persists, contact support for further assistance and keep photos of the wiring ready to speed up troubleshooting.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting Furnace Heating Issues

chunks.content: This article helps troubleshoot common cooling issues on an ecobee thermostat. When the thermostat is requesting cooling, the snowflake icon will usually be blue or a blue line will appear around the perimeter depending on the model.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting Cooling Issues

chunks.section_title: When ecobee is not requesting cooling
chunks.content: If the thermostat is not requesting cooling even though the indoor temperature is above the set temperature, first confirm that cooling works by using Test Mode on the thermostat.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting Cooling Issues

chunks.content: Select Cool Stage 1 On, or Heat Pump Cool Stage 1 if you have a heat pump, and wait two minutes. Then confirm that the outside unit is running and that cool air is coming from the vents. If the outside unit does not run or there is no airflow, continue troubleshooting the wiring and configuration.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting Cooling Issues

chunks.section_title: If the outdoor unit runs but the air is not cool
chunks.content: If the outdoor unit is running but the air in the home is not cool, the cause may be extreme outdoor temperatures or an issue with HVAC equipment or ventilation. Monitor the home over a longer period of time and consult an HVAC technician if needed. If you are unsure whether the equipment is actually running, contact support.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting Cooling Issues

chunks.content: Confirm the ecobee is set to Auto or Cool mode. On the main screen, a snowflake appears in Cool mode, and a half snowflake half flame appears in Auto mode. If the system is not in one of those modes, it will not call for cooling. Also check the Cool Differential, because the home temperature must be above the set temperature by the configured amount before cooling is requested.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting Cooling Issues

chunks.content: Check the Compressor Min Outdoor Temperature threshold. If the outside temperature is below this threshold, the compressor will not be asked to run. On most ecobee thermostats, the setting is found under Main Menu > General Settings > Settings > Installation Settings > Thresholds > Compressor Min Outdoor Temperature. On Smart Thermostat Lite and Essential models, the path is Main Menu > Settings > Installation Settings > Thresholds > Compressor Min Outdoor Temperature.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting Cooling Issues

chunks.content: If the thermostat is configured to control a Fresh Air Ventilator system, Free Cooling may be used to cool the home instead of running the AC. You can disable it from the thermostat under Main Menu > General Settings > System > Ventilator > Free Cooling, or on Smart Thermostat Lite under Main Menu > System > Ventilator > Free Cooling.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting Cooling Issues

chunks.section_title: When there is no airflow or no Cool option
chunks.content: If the ecobee is requesting cooling but there is no airflow from the vents or no Cool option appears, check the wiring. Remove the thermostat from the wall and gently confirm that each wire is secure, with special attention to the Y1 wire or the PEK terminal if a Power Extender Kit is installed. Reseat any loose wire, then take a photo of the wiring if everything appears secure.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting Cooling Issues

chunks.content: Verify the configuration under Main Menu > General Settings > Settings > Installation Settings > Equipment > Wiring, or on Smart Thermostat Lite and Essential models under Main Menu > Settings > Installation Settings > Equipment > Wiring. The highlighted wires should match the wiring behind the thermostat. If they do not, choose Reconfigure Equipment and follow the setup steps again. Then use Test Mode to confirm airflow and outdoor unit operation.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting Cooling Issues

chunks.section_title: If the configuration is correct but cooling still fails
chunks.content: Something else may be preventing the system from running smoothly. Check for water buildup by looking for the thermostat powering off or rebooting, moisture around the air handler, an overflowing condensate pan, or water damage near the drain line. Inspect the float switch, drain pan, and condensate drain line for clogs. Turn off HVAC power at the breaker before cleaning the drain pan or clearing clogs.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting Cooling Issues

chunks.content: Consult the HVAC manual or manufacturer resources for additional troubleshooting steps such as checking the compressor for refrigerant leaks, clearing ice buildup, replacing the AC filter, or cleaning the compressor. If the issue continues, contact support or an HVAC technician.
chunks.title: Troubleshooting Cooling Issues

chunks.content: If your ecobee thermostat has a black screen and will not turn on, follow these steps to troubleshoot the problem.
chunks.title: How to troubleshoot ecobee thermostat power issues

chunks.section_title: If you just installed your ecobee
chunks.content: Confirm the wiring first. For models with Rc and Rh connectors, make sure the R wire is securely connected to Rc. For models with just R, make sure the R wire is securely connected. Make sure the C wire is connected to the C connector on the thermostat. If you do not have a C wire, check for a spare wire and connect it to the C connector on the HVAC control board. If no spare wire is available, use the Power Extender Kit.
chunks.title: How to troubleshoot ecobee thermostat power issues

chunks.content: If a Power Extender Kit was used, verify the wiring matches the ecobee model. For most models, R from the PEK goes to RC, G goes to C, W goes to W1, and Y goes to the PEK connector. For Smart Thermostat Enhanced, R from the PEK goes to R, G goes to C, W goes to W1, and Y goes to the PEK connector. For Smart Thermostat Essential, R goes to R, G goes to C, W goes to W1, and Y goes to G or PEK. Also ensure the C wire from the PEK is connected to the C connector on the HVAC control board.
chunks.title: How to troubleshoot ecobee thermostat power issues

chunks.content: Smart Thermostat Lite and Smart Thermostat Essential do not come with a Power Extender Kit and may need to be purchased separately.
chunks.title: How to troubleshoot ecobee thermostat power issues

chunks.content: Check that the ecobee is properly placed on the thermostat base. Remove the thermostat, push excess wires back into the wall, and make sure there are no gaps between the ecobee and the base. You should hear an audible click when the thermostat connects.
chunks.title: How to troubleshoot ecobee thermostat power issues

chunks.content: Confirm that the HVAC system is turned on at the circuit breaker. If the HVAC was opened for wiring changes, make sure it was closed correctly. Check the fuse on the furnace control board, usually 3 or 5 amp, and replace it if blown. If possible, test voltage between RC or R and C at the ecobee with a voltmeter; it should read between 24 and 29VAC.
chunks.title: How to troubleshoot ecobee thermostat power issues

chunks.section_title: If the ecobee was working before
chunks.content: The ecobee has no internal power source and depends on HVAC equipment for power. If the HVAC has no power, the ecobee will not turn on. Check for a tripped breaker and reset it. Inspect the furnace control board for a blown 3 or 5 amp fuse and replace it with a fuse of the same amperage. Using the wrong fuse can damage the equipment.
chunks.title: How to troubleshoot ecobee thermostat power issues

chunks.content: If the ecobee loses power or reboots during heating, check the high limit switch on the furnace and consider replacing the furnace filter. When a furnace overheats, the high limit sensor can trip and turn off the furnace and the ecobee. The fan blower may continue running to cool the system, or the system may not do anything until it is reset or has cooled down sufficiently. If overheating continues after changing the filter, consult the furnace manual or contact an HVAC technician.
chunks.title: How to troubleshoot ecobee thermostat power issues

chunks.content: If the ecobee loses power or reboots during cooling, check the HVAC drainage. Air conditioning creates condensation that should drain away normally. If water cannot flow freely because of dirt, debris, or a blockage in the drip pan or condensate line, a wet switch or float switch may cut power to the HVAC unit to prevent flooding and damage. Refer to the HVAC manual for how to clear blockages and restore water flow.
chunks.title: How to troubleshoot ecobee thermostat power issues

chunks.content: If possible, test voltage between RC or R and C with a voltmeter; it should read between 24 and 29VAC. If you still cannot resolve the issue, consult the HVAC manual or contact an HVAC technician. When reaching out to support, have a photo of the original thermostat wiring and a photo of how the ecobee is wired.
chunks.title: How to troubleshoot ecobee thermostat power issues
